channel.title: Microbial Metallomics — Research
channel.description: New writing, research summaries, and paper reviews from Microbial Metallomics.

item.title: Six Decades of Fertilizer Use Built a Legacy of Cadmium, Nickel, and Lead in Soils and Diets
item.description: Preprint — A food metallomics review (1960–2025) showing how phosphate and urea fertilizers loaded soils, crops, and diets with cadmium, nickel, lead, and chromium.

item.title: Heavy Metals and Microbial Metallomics: A New Framework for the US Obesity Epidemic
item.description: Preprint — How dietary cadmium, arsenic, lead, and nickel may disrupt gut microbial metallomics—driving dysbiosis, inflammation, and insulin resistance behind obesity.

item.title: Developmental Readiness Is Not Toxicokinetic Safety: Heavy Metals in Vegetable-Based Baby Foods
item.description: Preprint — Developmental readiness for solids does not ensure toxicokinetic safety: leafy greens, brassicas and root crops concentrate lead, cadmium and arsenic in baby foods.

item.title: Concentration-Based Heavy Metal Standards to Reduce Real Exposure in Infant and Child Foods
item.description: Standard — HMTc 2026 sets concentration-based, as-sold action levels for lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury, nickel and other heavy metals in infant and child foods.

item.title: Nickel as a Catalytic Driver of Necrotizing Enterocolitis
item.description: Journal article — Dietary nickel in infant formula may activate nickel-dependent microbial enzymes (urease, glyoxalase I) that drive necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm infants.

item.title: A Unified Model for FIP-Associated Gingivitis in Cats: Disrupting Microbial Shielding and Restoring Nutritional Immunity
item.description: Journal article — How itraconazole and lactoferrin may treat FIP-linked gingivitis in cats by disrupting polymicrobial biofilms and restoring metal-based nutritional immunity.

item.title: Microbiome Medicine Journal: Restoring Causal Structure to Disease Through Microbial Metallomics
item.description: Journal — Microbiome Medicine Journal Vol. I sets out a mechanism-first framework linking microbial ecology, host metallome regulation, and metal dyshomeostasis to disease.

item.title: From Dysbiosis to Dyshomeostasis: Reframing Parkinson's Through a Metallomic–Microbiome Lens
item.description: Journal article — A metallomics framework reframes Parkinson's as metal dyshomeostasis: iron, manganese, copper, zinc and nickel dysregulation drives dysbiosis and neuron loss.

item.title: The MC1R–Parkinson's Link May Be a Metallomic Story, Not a Cosmetic One
item.description: Journal article — A hypothesis linking MC1R red-hair variants to Parkinson's risk via melanin-metal chemistry: how copper, zinc, and iron shape neuromelanin's redox buffering.

item.title: Parkinson's Disease as a Disorder of Metal Dyshomeostasis Amplified by Microbial Ecology
item.description: Journal article — A synthesis framework proposing Parkinson's disease begins with heavy-metal dyshomeostasis that drives ferroptosis, gut dysbiosis, and α-synuclein pathology.
